name: Sun
description: A yellow dwarf star that holds 99.8% of the Solar System's mass. Sunlight takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach Earth.

name: Mercury
description: The smallest planet and the closest to the Sun. With almost no atmosphere to hold heat, its surface swings from about 430 °C by day to −180 °C at night.

name: Venus
description: Nearly Earth's size, but a thick carbon-dioxide atmosphere traps so much heat that it is the hottest planet. It spins backwards, so the Sun rises in the west.

name: Earth
description: The only world known to host life, with liquid water covering about 71% of its surface. Its 23.4° tilt gives us the seasons.

name: Mars
description: A cold desert world whose red colour comes from iron oxide in its dust. It has the tallest volcano in the Solar System, Olympus Mons, about 22 km high.

name: Jupiter
description: The largest planet, more than twice as massive as all the others combined. Its Great Red Spot is a storm wider than Earth.

name: Saturn
description: Famous for its bright rings of ice and rock. It is the least dense planet, less dense than water.

name: Uranus
description: An ice giant tipped on its side, with an axial tilt of about 98°. Each pole gets around 42 years of sunlight followed by 42 years of darkness.

name: Neptune
description: The most distant planet, with the fastest winds in the Solar System at over 2,000 km/h. It was predicted by mathematics before anyone saw it in 1846.
